designSummary: Step 1 is descriptive. Step 2 has two candidate analyses, both specified now so the design choice cannot change them.
sampleSize: Step 1 includes every patient in the four-week window (about 1,150); if 70 percent have calculable time in range, the 95 percent confidence interval is about plus or minus 2.6 percentage points, precise enough to apply criterion k1 at each clinic. For step 2, with a between-patient standard deviation of time in range of about 20 percentage points, detecting a 5-point difference with 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 needs about 252 patients per approach in a randomised comparison, about 17 months of the clinic's 30 new referrals a month. A records comparison could include about 600 patients per approach at once, but its precision would not protect it from confounding by site.
primaryAnalysis: Step 1: proportion of patients with calculable time in range by clinic and testing mode, with Wilson 95 percent intervals. Step 2, records comparison: linear regression of time in range on approach adjusted for the four case-mix variables. Step 2, randomised comparison: difference in mean time in range with a 95 percent confidence interval.
secondaryAnalysis: Major bleeding and thromboembolic events per 100 patient-years by approach, descriptive only; distribution of test-to-entry delay where recorded; minutes per dosing decision by approach.
missingData: Patients without calculable time in range are counted and described by clinic and testing mode, never imputed; any step 2 analysis restricted to calculable patients reports the restriction and its size.
multiplicity: One primary outcome per step; secondary outcomes are descriptive and are not tested.
software: R, with extraction rules and analysis code archived before step 1 starts.
overfittingGuards: Outcome and case-mix variables fixed before any data are seen
Design chosen on calculability only, never on observed time-in-range values
Step 2 sample size fixed from the planning values stated here
summary: Step 1 estimates calculability to about 2.6 points; a randomised step 2 would need about 252 patients per approach.
